title: MSFS2024 Knowledge Cache
description:
A distilled cache of verified MSFS2024 development knowledge, gathered from the official SDK & docs, DevSupport, the local SDK, and community sources. Consult this before searching the web again. Every entry carries a Status and a Source so you always know what to trust.

This file is exposed to sessions as the `msfs2024-knowledge` reference (project `.opencode/opencode.json` + global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`) and backs up to an external drive.

usage.title: Using & contributing
rules: For any MSFS2024-specific question, `/read` this file first. If it answers with a solid `Status`, stop — no web research needed.
Adding knowledge: verify first via the fallback chain (local SDK → official docs/DevSupport → community), then append a dated entry. Never bulk paste docs — keep entries atomic, snippet-sized.

User-typed claims (maintainer statements) are taken as true exactly as stated — status `user-typed (authoritative)`; additions from external files (dumps, pastes) go through the full verification chain first.
Every entry MUST carry `Status`, `Source`, `Added`. Status values:

Categories are the entries of the `categories` array, numbered via their `number` field (1–18); entries are objects in `category.entries`. An entry that fits more than one category lives once in its home category and is listed in each other relevant category's `crossReferences` array as `{title, entryId}` (title + entryId only). A category with no primary entries keeps a non-null `reserved` note so agents know the gap is deliberate, not missing.

entries.title: Custom vegetation assets for MSFS 2024 — addon Vegetation material (Foliage Mask slot); legacy Tree/Vegetation materials + Foliage Mask R/G/B (Mask/Translucency/WindMask) marked 'not currently used'; no wind/seasons for custom trees; community path: Speedtree + plane-atlas foliage; fs-base ships pines
entries.claim:
Deep-dive research (source C) on **creating custom vegetation assets for MSFS 2024** — the official docs are a dead end for wind/season-reactive custom trees (legacy paths all marked not-currently-used), which explains why this topic is hard to find:

**1. The addon ships a dedicated Vegetation material (fact cited, SDK).** `MSFS2024_Vegetation` (`blender/material/msfs_material_vegetation.py`): attributes = Base Color (+ texture), Emissive color/scale + day/night multipliers (+ texture), Alpha Mode (**defaults to OPAQUE**), Render Parameters (Draw Order Offset, No Cast Shadow, Double Sided, Flip Backface Normal, Disable Motion Blur, Roughness/Occlusion/Normal scale, Detail UV/Normal scale, Detail Blend Threshold), UV offset/tiling/rotation + clamp, Collision Material / Road Collision Material flags; textures = Base Color, OMR, Normal, Emissive, Detail Color/OMR/Normal, Blend Mask, **Foliage Mask**, Occlusion UV2. Registered as material type `msfs_vegetation` (`blender/utils/msfs_material_utils.py:42`); exported with material code `Vegetation` (`io/com/extensions/material/asobo_material_code.py:27,53`).

**2. The 2020-era wind/translucency channels are OFF in 2024 (fact cited, official docs).** The FlightSim Materials / Textures / Parameters reference pages mark the entire legacy family as *"not currently used in the simulation"*: Tree material (no params), Vegetation material (only **Translucency** param — *not currently used*), Windflex (Move Detail Normal — *not currently used*), and the **Foliage Mask(R) Translucency(G) WindMask(B)** texture (Tree, Vegetation block, alongside Base Color / OMR / Normal / Emissive / Detail x3 / Blend Mask / Occlusion UV2) — the wind-mask channel exists in the spec but is documented as inactive. Consequence: **no documented engine hook makes custom trees react to wind/seasons in 2024**.

**3. Community reality (empirical).** DevSupport 17494: custom (vegetation-polygon) trees **don't move / don't react to seasons** while sim trees do — "break the immersion tremendously". DevSupport 17365: vegetation rendering issues through buildings + unpopulated vegetation polygons. Working community pipeline (FSDeveloper 456116): **trees built in Speedtree, textured/exported through Blender, foliage as simple planes with an atlas texture**. Alpha/glass-era tricks: FakeTerrain material + Mask mode for tree alpha (FSDeveloper 454079, 2020-era). Known artifacts on foliage planes: sun/light reflection (FSDeveloper 457547), cross-plane shading (455131).

**4. Sourcing — native assets are good (empirical, channel).** Channel (25/04/2024 — losconosciuto + mamu82): "nella fs-base ci sono dei pini decenti" — **fs-base ships decent pines** (pines/larches fit alpine/taiga scenery); reusing native fs-base trees beats building every tree.

**5. Controlling native vegetation around your custom trees (empirical).** Native trees are placed procedurally; clearing them at a location uses the project's **vegetation override** (DevSupport 18406 snippet — 'vegetation override… turn off flightsim'); FSDeveloper 460420 shows 2024 exclude/override polygons not always removing third-party-scenery trees.

**Negative evidence (inferred):** no Asobo ModelBehaviorDefs template exists for vegetation wind (scan of AircraftTypes/Misc found only aircraft wind vars + wind turbine) — 2024 vegetation wind/seasons are engine-internal for native trees, not an XML/behavior hook custom assets can subscribe to. Native 2024 tree tech (procedural species) remains engine-side.

entries.title: Scenery SimObjects read only global-scope variables — never the user aircraft's A: state
entries.claim:
Claim: RPN code on a scenery (non-aircraft) SimObject — animated hangar door, gate, windsock, character — cannot read the user aircraft's A: SimVars (`A:LIGHT LANDING`, `A:PLANE LATITUDE`, …). Aircraft-scoped A: variables have "no effect at all" there. What DOES evaluate:

- L: — cross-object channel (an aircraft or WorldScript writes, the scenery SimObject reads).
- E: — global environment/time vars (`E:LOCAL TIME`, `E:SIMULATION TIME`).
- A: — but only own-object or global/environmental state: `A:AMBIENT WIND *`, `A:AMBIENT TEMPERATURE`, `A:SEA LEVEL PRESSURE`, `A:AMBIENT PRECIP STATE`, `A:ANIMATION DELTA TIME` (confirmed working); one poster found "(A:SEA LEVEL PRESSURE…) is reading the pressure on the simobject, not on the aircraft".

Consequence: an "interactable hangar door opened because my plane is near/parked" can NOT condition directly on `(A:PLANE *)` inside the door's animation — the plane's state must be injected (see Pattern A / Pattern B below).
entries.status: `empirical` (multiple community posters, MSFS2020-confirmed, consistent with MSFS2024 behavior).
sources: FSDeveloper "Visibility" thread p.10 — https://www.fsdeveloper.com/forum/threads/visibility.449781/page-10

entries.title: Multiplayer Near/Far SimVar propagation — aircraft ↔ aircraft only (RESOLVED 2026-09-20)
entries.claim:
Official wording (docs, Simulation Variables → "Note On SimVars In Multiplayer"):

"Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 does not have the same concept of shared cockpit as previous versions, as such only a small number of variables are communicated between all aircraft … Near: these SimVars are transmitted to all aircraft within a 500m radius. Far: these SimVars are transmitted to all aircraft up to a maximum radius of 10,000m."

Resolution: the propagation is scoped to "all aircraft" — it exists so other aircraft instances can reproduce your lights/gear/surfaces. There is no official path for a scenery SimObject's RPN to read these (or any user-aircraft A:) values; the empirical record agrees (aircraft A: vars have "no effect at all" on scenery SimObjects — first entry). A scenery object that must react to the user plane has to use the Pattern A / Pattern B entries below (aircraft-written L: mirrors / WorldScript scenario trigger).

Near list (≤500 m): `GEAR_ANIMATION_POSITION`, `GEAR_POSITION`, `GEAR_*_STEER_ANGLE`, control-surface PCTs, `SIM ON GROUND`, `GENERAL ENG STARTER ACTIVE`, prop/turbofan animation vars (`PROP ROTATION ANGLE`, `TURB_ENG_N1`, `TURB_ENG_AFTERBURNER*`, …). Far list (≤10 km): `LIGHT_*` (nav/taxi/landing/strobe/beacon/logo/wing/states), `GENERAL ENG RPM` / `COMBUSTION` (+ sound PCT), `GROUND_VELOCITY`, rotor/disk vars, `SIM ON GROUND`.
entries.status: `fact (cited)` (official wording) → resolution `inferred` (official scoping + empirical "no effect" record; the docs never mention scenery SimObjects explicitly, so treat as "no" with high, not absolute, confidence).
sources: MSFS2024 docs Simulation Variables index, "Note On SimVars In Multiplayer" — https://docs.flightsimulator.com/msfs2024/html/6_Programming_APIs/SimVars/Simulation_Variables.htm

entries.title: 2020 → 2024 SimObject conversion quirks
entries.claim:
Conversion-relevant differences (2024 docs, "Using The SDK" → SimObjects):

- `.air` file removed: "`.air` files (FSX flight model configuration files) have been removed in favor of exposing all flight model parameters in plain text `.cfg` files" (`aircraft.cfg` / `sim.cfg` cover everything).
- ModelBehaviors XML named after the glTF: "this link is done through an `*.xml` file which is named after the name of its accompanying `*.gltf` file" — `MODEL.gltf` ↔ `MODEL.xml`.
- ≥1 asset group per package: "Each package will require one or more asset group to be a valid package"; an aircraft typically has several (SimObject + ModelLib + MaterialLib asset groups).
- "One SimObject per package" (2020-era) superseded: 2024 packages can hold any content mix — "a single project will have one or more independent packages… A package can contain any type of content supported by the simulation… defined by adding one or more Asset Groups". (Docs never state the supersession explicitly — `inferred` from the cited structure.)
entries.status: `fact (cited)` (docs) for the first three; 2020-claim supersession `inferred` (derived from the cited 2024 package structure).
sources: https://docs.flightsimulator.com/msfs2024/flighting/introduction/using-the-sdk/ (SimObjects → Structure / Model Behaviors; Creating Your First Package)

entries.title: Scenery collision boxes — don't Apply transforms, keep colliders outside the scaled hierarchy; 2024 colliders are children of the object auto-fitted to its bounding box; large world scale breaks collision detection
entries.claim:
Channel rule (29/05/2024 — losconosciuto asks: "le collision box funzionano bene? Non sclera non applicando la scala?" — do collision boxes work well, doesn't it scale wrong if you don't apply the scale? → mamu82: "Sì, solo non Applica le transform a tutto, loro le devi tenere fuori" — **yes, just don't Apply transforms to everything — keep the collision boxes outside [the scaled hierarchy]**). losconosciuto: "Perfetto!". Practical workflow for scenery with colliders:

**don't Apply transforms (Ctrl+A) to the whole hierarchy** — the MSFS colliders are auto-fitted children whose local transform must stay clean; and **keep collision boxes outside the scaled object chain**.

**Mechanic, official (fact cited):** MSFS 2024 colliders are added via the Add menu (Shift+A); when an object is active, the collision is **added as a child of the active object and automatically scaled to match its bounding box**; the docs stress "**IMPORTANT! Collisions are added as children of the active object. This is required for correct export**" (Blender Plugin Properties — Simple Shape Collisions). Simple-shape collisions are **curve objects with a dedicated Geometry Nodes modifier** that defines the collision export properties; the addon ships the asset-library node groups `.MSFS_2024_Collision` (Collision Type: Road Collider / Ground Collider) and `.MSFS_2024_Bounding_Volume` (`datafiles/asset_library.py:11-24`).

**Why scale breaks collisions (docs, fact cited):** the engine supports **box, sphere and cylinder colliders** (recommended over mesh/material collisions, esp. for scenery elements and airports); mesh collisions have a 65K-triangle limit (warning past 4096) and — the key line — "**Collisions will not be properly detected if the vertices are too far from each other, in particular when the object has been scaled by a large amount in the world**, or its geometry hasn't got enough subdivisions" (Collision Handling). Large scaling is the *documented* failure vector — the channel rule sidesteps it by keeping colliders out of scaled chains.

**Exporter side (fact cited):** multi-export merges meshes and **reparents non-mesh objects (lights, collisions …)** (`io/exp/multi_export.py:739`) — colliders travel as independent objects with their own transform contract; baking parent transforms (Ctrl+A applies to hierarchical descendants) or scaling the parent chain distorts that clean transform.

**Scope + version notes:** only **static (Scenery) objects detect collisions with the user aircraft** (docs); the Collision Handling page is legacy large-scale landscape guidance, superseded for large-scale modelling by **SimProp Containers** (2024). Community corroboration that collision export is exporter-version-sensitive: DevSupport 17794 — simple collisions failed in SU5 exporter v6.4.7 on Blender 3.6.
entries.status: `fact (cited)` (official docs — Blender Plugin Properties: child-of-object auto-fit + GN modifier colliders; Collision Handling: shape recommendation, 65K limit, large-scale breakage, static-only, SimPropContainer supersession; SDK addon: asset_library collision node groups + multi_export reparenting) + `empirical` (channel-tested workflow rule, 29/05/2024).

entries.title: Split glTF model + animations — <MergeModel> merges an external animation .gltf per LOD (deprecated <AnimationFileList>; merge keyed by ASOBO unique id)
entries.claim:
MSFS 2024 pattern for characters / any bone-animated object: the model (`.gltf`) and its animations live in SEPARATE glTF files, merged at load through the model XML. Each `<LOD>` of `[model].xml` can contain one or more `<MergeModel>` elements naming extra glTF files ("the different animation and/or submodel gLTF files that should be used for the SimObject over the different <LOD /> elements"); paths are relative to the model XML location. Merge order: base `ModelFile` first, then each `<MergeModel>` in document order (docs example — FireTruck LOD with four submodel parts, then `<MergeModel>..\animation\FireTruck.gltf</MergeModel>`).

This replaced the 2020-era `<AnimationFileList>` element, now deprecated: "the code put in place to deal with submodels is also applicable when working with animations, and has deprecated the <AnimationFileList> element". Submodel merging is also more efficient — "the submodel data is shared across all models that use it, whereas the <AnimationFileList> code duplicated the animation data".

Merge mechanics (Submodel Merging page — BETA): merging happens by **unique id**, NOT by node name (ASOBO_unique_id glTF extension; enable it on both base and merged exports; ids default to node name; duplicate ids → warning). Animations merge by NAME — an animation name already present in the destination is merged/ignored (the docs say this will become an error). Materials are NOT merged. Conflicts abort the merge: same node carrying objects in both models, or mismatched parent-chain ids; name mismatches only warn. Restrictions: all merged files must be in the SAME project; skinned submodels must export with their bones; at least one common ancestor between submodel mesh and skin bones; max ONE skin root ("More than one root node for the skin" error); never export animations for a node in more than one merged model; never export meshes in more than one merged model. Official framing: "sub-models can only be used to attach a relatively simple model with animations and a small amount of behavior logic in it".

Shipped example — SDK Bears sample (`Samples\DevmodeProjects\SimObjects\Animals\Bears`): `GrizzlyBear.xml` / `BlackBear.xml` each carry 4 LODs with `<LOD minSize="6" ModelFile="GrizzlyBear_LOD00.gltf">` + `<MergeModel>..\animation\Bears.gltf</MergeModel>`, plus `<AnimationInclude><Include File=".\..\animations.xml"/></AnimationInclude>`. The `animation\Bears.gltf` ships ONLY the node hierarchy + animation clips (no meshes; ASOBO_unique_id extension; exporter stamp "babylon.js glTF exporter for 3dsmax 2022" — but a Blender source ships at `Sources\Art\Blender\Bear_Adult.blend`). `animations.xml` composes clips: `<Animation name="Walk" type="Standard" typeParam="random"/>` + `Idle1/2/3`, then an `<AnimGraph>` with `<BlendTreeState>` Idle (3 looped clips) and Walk (condition `(A:GROUND VELOCITY, METERS PER SECOND)`) plus A:-based `<Transition>`s.

entries.title: Scenery animation scope — scenery objects CAN animate: Standard `<Animation type="Standard" typeParam="AutoPlay">` plays on render on plain scenery objects (lighthouse mirror, bone/armature glTF); sim-reactive animation (wind → windsock, aircraft → jetway) is the Scenery SimObj path (category=StaticObject, DistanceToNotAnimate)
entries.claim:
MSFS 2024 scenery has TWO delivery paths, and BOTH can carry animations — 'static scenery object' is a CLASS of object ('one that has no animations or interactions within the simulation'), a definition, NOT a ban on animated scenery (maintainer correction 2026-09-23: 'Scenery Objects CAN and are frequently animated'):

- **Plain scenery object (Scenery Editor / ModelLib asset group)** — CAN be animated: its model XML supports `<Animation>` elements and the animation plays on render: `<Animation name="Ambient" guid="{...}" type="Standard" typeParam="AutoPlay" />` — AutoPlay = 'the animation will run when the object is rendered' (render-driven, no SimObject needed). This is the classic lighthouse-mirror / radar-antenna / windmill pattern: node rotation keyframes AND bone/armature glTF animations both play (maintainer: simple animated objects + 'more complex bone and armature animations'). ModelInfo children include `<Animation>`, `<NodeAnimation>`, `<AnimationEvent>`, `<AnimGraph>` — none restricted to SimObjects (model-xml-properties:50-62). The Scenery Editor instancing rule only makes sense if scenery objects can be animated: 'For an object to be instanced, it **cannot be animated** nor have multiple nodes' (scenery-objects:99).

entries.title: Random looping-animation selection — `<AnimGraph>` `<BlendTreeState doBlend="FALSE">` weighted-random next clip per loop end; `typeParam="AutoPlay,Random"` for autoplay + random start frame
entries.claim:
The XML-level answers to '4-5 looping animations on one object, pick a random one' — all from Model Animation Definitions (elements live in `[model].xml`, a shared `animations.xml`, or `<Behaviors>`/`<Component>`):

- **Scope (2026-09-23, scenery correction):** the single-clip Standard flags below — `typeParam="AutoPlay,Random"` (autoplay + random start frame) — run on PLAIN scenery objects (render-driven, no SimObject needed); blend-tree machinery DOES appear in scenery model XML too — the official windsock example puts `<AnimGraph>` → `<BlendTreeState>` with six Standard clips straight in the scenery model XML (scenery-model-xml-and-cfg-setup:141-180), BUT that state is threshold-driven (`<Value>(A:AMBIENT WIND VELOCITY, KNOTS)</Value>` + per-clip `threshold`) — i.e. the doBlend=TRUE continuous rule, NOT random selection. The doBlend="FALSE" weighted-random CLIP SELECTION below is documented on the AnimGraph/SIMOBJECT path — docs: 'The AnimGraph system is mostly used by Living Thing SimObjects' (animation-xml-properties:146); a scenery character that needs random CLIP selection uses the Scenery SimObj wrapper (category=StaticObject).
- **Random start frame + autoplay on a single clip**: `<Animation name="Ambient" guid="{...}" type="Standard" typeParam="AutoPlay,Random" />` — AutoPlay: 'the animation will run when the object is rendered'; Random: 'the animation will be started at a random point along its timeline'. (Optional FrameRate=N — the FrameRate reference value, default 18 fps, a speed scalar — then requires `length`.)
- **Weighted random pick between multiple looping clips**: `<AnimGraph>` → ONE `<BlendTreeState>` listing ALL the clips with `doBlend="FALSE"` ('if this is set to FALSE, then animations will only change when the current one is finished playing, and the subsequent animation to use will be chosen **at random**, based on the `weight` attribute'). Each clip is an `<Animation guid="..." loop="True" speed="1" weight="0.2" />` — weight between 0 and 1, 'the higher the value, the more likely the animation is to be chosen'. With `loop="True"` on every clip the state cycles through random picks forever — no code, no SimVar input needed. This is exactly the '4/5 looping animations, random one every loop' pattern.
- **Conditions / other circumstances**: `<Transition start=... end=...>` — automatic with `<Condition>` RPN 'evaluated every frame' (docs example: `(A:SURFACE RELATIVE GROUND SPEED, METERS PER SECOND) 0.1 >` — swap when ground speed exceeds 0.1 m/s), or automatic by `ExitTime` ratio (1.0 = at end of the current animation, 0.5 = halfway, 2.5 = after 2.5 looped iterations); a transition with NEITHER Condition NOR ExitTime is '**manual**' — only fires when code/script requests the other state (e.g. `SimMission.PlayBlendTreeStateAction`; `FireEventOnEnd` makes the action wait for clip end). Within a state, `doBlend="TRUE"` + `<Value>` RPN + per-clip `threshold` blends clips continuously instead of random-switching.
- RPN scope reminder: on scenery-placed SimObjs `<Condition>`/`<Value>` code can only read the object's own / global state (wind, time, `A:ANIMATION DELTA TIME`, L: mirrors written by aircraft/WorldScript) — never the user aircraft's A: scope (see the Official corroboration entry + variable-scope entries).
- First-pick caveat: the docs define the weighted-random draw only for picks AFTER an animation ends; which clip plays when the state is first entered / object first renders is not specified — open question.

entries.title: Creating a custom animal from scratch (2024) — Living Thing SimObject: sim.cfg (category=Animal|FlyingAnimal) + animations.xml AnimGraph Walk/Idle on GROUND VELOCITY + Scenery Editor SimObj spawn points (Bears sample); default wildlife spawns as Living World entities, not via LWcfg.xml
entries.claim:
Deep-dive research (source C, 2026-09-23) on **adding a custom animal to MSFS 2024 post-export** — the user asked for the full practical pipeline (walking animation + random wandering around spawn points, like MSFS 2020 wildlife). All paths verified against the official docs + the shipped **BearsSampleProject** (the canonical Living-Thing template).

**1. Animals are 'Living Things' SimObjects — NOT Living World config.** Living Things docs: "the different living things available in the simulation are configured as SimObjects", split into Humans / Animals (ground: elephants, crabs, pigs) / Flying Animals (seagulls, bats, sparrows); a water animal (whale) is a **Boat** SimObject instead. They ship as `sim.cfg` + model + texture + (usually) animation, optionally `ai.cfg`, `camara.cfg`, `navigation_graph.cfg`. The 2024 `LWcfg.xml` (Living World Config) covers ONLY road traffic, leisure boats and airport life (vehicles + human characters) — **animals are not listed there**; default wildlife spawns independently as Living World entities (DevSupport 11803, empirical: "Animals now are spawned as Living World", visible in DevMode under debug SimObjects Living World). TL;DR: a custom animal is a normal SimObject package you place yourself, not a Living World config edit.

**2. Package layout (Bears sample — `PackageSources\SimObjects\Animals\MyCompany_Bears\`).** Top folder: `sim.cfg` + `animations.xml` (shared by all variations); per-variation subfolders `model.<X>\model.cfg` + `[model].xml` + LOD glTF, `texture.<X>\texture.cfg` + textures; shared `animation\Bears.gltf` + `animation\Bears.bin` (no meshes, ASOBO_unique_id) merged per-LOD via `<MergeModel>..\animation\Bears.gltf</MergeModel>` and included via `<AnimationInclude><Include File=".\..\animations.xml"/></AnimationInclude>` — the split-mesh/animations pattern (see the Split glTF entry). The SimObj Objects docs add that files for a *scenery* SimObject must live in a folder literally called **Landmarks** (the 'folder the simulation will look for when generating SimObjects for use in scenery'); the Bears animal sample instead uses the `SimObjects\Animals\...` Living-Things path ('This SimObject can be used anywhere in the world').

**3. sim.cfg — the movement/AI-side sections.** `[VERSION]`; `[fltsim.N]` variations (title/model/texture/animation; numbers can't be skipped; `model=BlackBear` → folder `model.BlackBear`); `[General]` `category=Animal` (REQUIRED — "will tell the simulation what other parameters to expect and initialise certain internal parameters"; use `FlyingAnimal` for birds — docs default `DistanceToNotAnimate`: FlyingAnimals 250 m, all others 1000 m; the Bears sample sets a custom 1500); `[contact_points] wheel_radius=1 / static_pitch=0.0 / static_cg_height=0` (ground resting); `[DesignSpecs] max_speed_mph=15 + acceleration_constants/deceleration_constants` (0.3/0.4, 0.2/0.4); `[WAYPOINT] CanReverse=0`. These are the parameters the ground AI uses to move the animal on the ground.

**4. animations.xml — Walk↔Idle AnimGraph driven by GROUND VELOCITY + random start frame.** `<Animation name="Walk" type="Standard" typeParam="random"/>` (random start frame!) + three `<Animation name="Idle1..3" type="Standard"/>`; then `<AnimGraph>`: `<DefaultState name="Idle"/>`; `<BlendTreeState name="Idle" doBlend="False">` listing the three Idle clips `loop="True" speed="1"` (the **doBlend=FALSE weighted-random next-clip machinery** from the E2 entry — Living Things are SimObjects, so the SimObject-path AnimGraph applies) + `<BlendTreeState name="Walk">` with `<Value>(A:GROUND VELOCITY, METERS PER SECOND)</Value>`; `<Transition start="Idle" end="Walk"><Condition>(A:GROUND VELOCITY, METERS PER SECOND) 0.1 ></Condition></Transition>` and the reverse `< 0.1`. Result: the animal plays random idle clips when stopped and the walk clip (random start frame) whenever the sim moves it — exactly 'old MSFS 2020 animals' style wandering, with `DistanceToNotAnimate` powering down both ModelBehaviors and animation when far (on return the animation jumps to the frame it should be on; `ANIMATION DELTA TIME` reports the skipped time).

**5. Spawn points — Scenery Editor → SimObj Objects.** Project Editor → Add Asset Group → Custom → asset type **SimObject** → add the files (model/glTF+xml+cfg, textures, animations bin, sim.cfg) → check AssetDir/OutputDir → build. In the Scenery Editor, the **SimObj Objects** object type lists SimObjects from installed packages ("ground vehicles, marshallers, animals, etc... are all SimObjects"); click Add, place with Translate/Rotation/Scale gizmos or **One-Click Placing** — each placed instance IS a spawn point (Snap To Ground enabled by default so it stays glued to terrain; Snap To Normal orients to the ground surface). Per-instance options: Assign Instance ID (guid — for mission/WorldScript spawning), Replace With…, and Convert To SimPropContainer (SimPropHolders can then spawn it with an optimized spawn probability). To verify your placed animals: DevMode debug shows default wildlife under SimObjects Living World; place your own instances and check the Behaviors/animations tool.

**6. Community reality (empirical).** DevSupport 11803 complains the Bears sample is minimal ('teaches nothing' — it deliberately stays simple for SDK beginners; per the Asobo reply it's aimed at people starting with MSFS); commercial animal packs exist (SoFly 'Animals for MSFS'); FSDeveloper marketplace-acceptability thread: "it is not permitted to add any animals or MS/Asobo planes as static decorations in your custom scenery" (marketplace rule of thumb — use your own models, or place SimObjects that stay dynamic). What remains undocumented: the exact wander logic of a placed Animal SimObject (see the linked Open Question).

entries.title: AutoLOD — Simplygon integrated LOD generation (2024)
entries.claim:
The 2024 build pipeline integrates the Simplygon SDK for automatic LOD generation ("AutoLOD"), applied per ModelLib asset group. Requirements and behavior:

- DevMode: "Debug LODs" window + "Enable Force Active LOD" to preview LODs.
- Docs note manually authored LODs generally give better results — use AutoLOD as the convenience path (exporter-side: 2024 Blender exporter "Enable Auto LOD" exports LOD0 only — see exporter entry above).

entries.title: KTX2 / KTX2P — marketplace vs community texture compile (2024)
entries.claim:
The Package Tool (in-sim build automation) compiles `*.gltf → *.glb`, `*.png → *.ktx2` and `*.xml → *.bgl` at build. Texture facts (official):

- Marketplace-ingested builds produce non-standard KTX2: "there are circumstances where these files are non-standard and use a propriety format … This happens when a project is built for ingestion into the Marketplace specifically" — not editable/viewable like normal KTX2.
- Community KTX2 are standard compliant ("as they do not go through marketplace ingestion"); ingested packages become standard compliant via the VFS Projector.
- Pixel values are not directly comparable to the source PNG/JPG after build ("pixel data is modified for consumption by the games shaders") — for community and marketplace builds.
- KTX2P is purely a streaming optimization: packs several related KTX2 files (e.g. albedo/norm/comp/emissive) so they stream in a single HTTP request; if absent, the sim falls back to the regular KTX2. If you modify KTX2 post-build but leave the KTX2P, the sim may use the old data — remove the KTX2P (post-build KTX2 edits are strongly discouraged).

Channel observation (Feb 2025, fs-sdk, single poster): marketplace builds came out roughly 2× the size, textures left uncompressed for streaming — `empirical`, not doc-confirmed (docs attribute streaming to KTX2P instead).

entries.title: LOD workflow & policy — 2020-era per-collection export loop (SU5 textureless last LOD) vs strict 2024 rules (max 7 LODs, screen-size vertex budgets, ≤50% per step)
entries.claim:
Channel workflow (ri-creativity, 31/01/2022, MSFS2020-SU5 era — losconosciuto): manual LOD export loop with the 2020 exporter — **Selected Only always on**; export everything together, then per LOD: show only that LOD's collection (`1`, `2`… on the numpad), press Q (export operator), **export glTF overwriting with the Generate XML and Generate LODs flags unchecked** — settings persist between LODs, so each subsequent LOD only needs the collection switch + Q. On the last LOD, **enable Vertex coloring** — because after Sim Update 5 the platform stopped allowing textures on the final LOD ("da dopo il sim update 5, hanno cambiato le politiche" — "sul LOD più basso le texture non te le lasciano più usare"). Poster also announced per-LOD textures halving resolution each step, expecting LOD triangle-count policing to arrive.

**Strict 2024 policy (official docs — LOD Technical Information + SDK lod_limits):**
- **Never exceed 7 LODs** (LOD0–LOD6), a hard cap. Recommended counts: **2** (traffic-cone class) to **5** (light aircraft), 7 only for very large/complex (airliner). If you think you need more, optimize better or split: SimProp Containers (scenery) / Sim Attachments (aircraft).
- **Step ratio: each next LOD will be at least 50% the polycount of the previous LOD** — i.e. ≥50% reduction per step, commonly down to 30%–40% retained.
- **Vertex budget by screen size** (SDK `lod_tools_msfs_2024/lod_limits.py` — ModelLodLimits): max 1 000 verts below 1% screen-size ratio, 2 500 at 1%, 250 000 at 100%, linear 0.01→1.0 and parabolic 1.0→100; `Default_LastLod_MinScreenSizeRatio = 0.001`, `Default_SecondToLastLod_MinScreenSizeRatio = 0.01`. Docs reference the same limits as "Vertex Count Limits" (LOD Selection System) — with the explicit warning that **hitting the limits is a trap**: optimize until no more vertices can be removed without losing shape, polycount will then always be under budget.
- **Recommended creation flow**: start from a fully optimized LOD0 → make the *most simplified* version as LOD1 (the engine removes objects below ~150 vertices by distance — "which is the minimum number of vertices an object can have before it will be removed by the engine from display") → package with minSize LOD0=1 / LOD1=0 → test where the swap happens → insert intermediate LODs only where transitions are visible.
- **Textures on far LODs**: reduce the material/texture count when moving to lower LODs and *re-use textures across LODs* — the 2024 docs do **not** carry the 2020-SU5 "no textures on the last LOD" hard rule (inferred: 2024 allows textures there, reduced/reused). Vertex-colored lowest LOD remains a valid community technique.
- Interiors (cockpits/holds/building interiors) need far fewer LODs; usually just LOD0 + the simplified last LOD. Remove geometry rather than simplify; automatic decimation tools "are *never* going to be as efficient, nor give the best results, as manual optimization" — consistent with the AutoLOD entry's note that manually authored LODs generally beat generated ones.

**2024 tooling (SDK addon)**: the manual overwrite-collection loop is replaced by the exporter's **LOD Groups** system (`ui/exp/lod_groups_panel.py`, `lod_groups_ops.py`, `io/exp/lod_groups.py` — `MultiExporterLODGroup`/`MultiExporterLOD`, `LOD_NAME_PATTERN` `_LOD{index}` naming, per-export-mode LOD assignment); the SDK also ships the companion addon **`lod_tools_msfs_2024`** (LOD viewer node groups/collections, active-LOD camera preview — `lod_viewer*.py`, `active_lod_viewer.py`, `lod_camera.py`, `lod_group_infos.py`, plus the `lod_limits.py` budget constants above). In-sim: DevMode → Debug LODs (LOD Screen Size / LOD Face Count) for testing swaps.

entries.title: Model optimization guidelines for MSFS — draw calls, texture budget, vertex economy and LOD practice
entries.claim:
Umbrella optimization guidelines for MSFS 2024 models (official 2024 docs + channel practice). Goal (docs — Modeling Technical Information): *reduce CPU/GPU costs, execution time and memory, while retaining visual quality*.

**Official performance metrics (docs, minimize all):** Texel Count (combined texture pixels; the compiled KTX2 size = GPU-memory size), Material Count, Mesh Object Count, Vertex Count, Face Count, skinned vertex/face counts, Texture Count, Node Count, Bone Count, collision vertex/face counts. **Draw-call rule (official):** draw calls are roughly *material count × meshes using them* — *"mesh instances with the same material are grouped in one draw call"*. Fewer materials → fewer draw calls; the last LOD should be **one draw call** (docs Scenery LODs: last LOD ≈ 150 triangles, 1 material, ideally shared textures; small emissive/metallic needs → tiny texture rather than a second material).

**Instancing (official):** placing the same model N times batches all instances into **one draw call** — non-skinned meshes only; skinned meshes never instance (a model mixing both still instances its non-skinned parts). Keep object structure so instances can merge.

**Channel workflow (ri-creativity, 17/12/2024 — mamu82):** in Blender use **one material per object** (e.g. a shed: wooden posts + corrugated roof share a single material; material separation done with **layer masks inside Substance Painter**, not Blender materials). Each Blender material = one texture set, and **more texture sets = more draw calls** ("Però aumenti le drawcalls"). Trade-off flagged by the same poster: one material/texture-set per object caps the resolution you can reach per part — "non necessariamente un materiale unico per ogni oggetto, dipende da che risultato vuoi ottenere in termini di risoluzione". Community resource shared in the thread: **FSDeveloper "Substance Painter export presets for MSFS"** (four SP export presets for MSFS 2020-aligned texture sets; usable as the base for 2024). Community priority rule of thumb (FSDeveloper 455936): minimize **draw calls > texture vertices > polygons**.

**Trim-sheet practice (channel, 19/12/2024 — salvuz, professional big-scale scenery developer, maintainer-confirmed @ INI Builds):** the standard practice for large scenery is **trim sheets** — several materials grouped onto **one texture arranged in rows, seamless in the horizontal direction so it can tile** ("raggruppo vari materiali in un'unica texture, disposta su righe e quindi seamless in orizzontale e posso fare tiling"); the sheet is then **shared across many models** ("posso condividere le texture su più modelli"), with **unique textures only for small/detailed hero objects**; **decals** are used for dirt and to break up / hide the tiling pattern when visible ("uso i decal per lo sporco e nascondere i pattern creati dal tiling se necessario"). Approach is mixed per building size ("dipende dalla grandezza dell'edificio") — e.g. four textures merged into one sheet. Community footprint: tiling textures as the package-size remedy (FSDeveloper 458792) and dirt decals over repeating textures (FSDeveloper 456437) corroborate the technique family.

**Texture budget (official Scenery LODs):** share textures between models/LODs; **remove textures not needed at distance** (e.g. the normal map) — and prefer *removing* over creating smaller-resolution variants (extra small textures increase total memory); use per-material appropriate resolutions (not all the same); prefer metallic/roughness **material parameters** over textures when possible; UV data is stored as **2-byte floats** post-compile → keep UV values 0–1 to preserve precision (tiled UVs: shift to a negative range, e.g. 0–10 → −5..5).

**Vertex economy (official):** model only what is visible at the typical viewing distance (scenery props are not aircraft); weld/merge (Blender Weld Modifier) before the end; remove never-visible polygons; beware **decal geometry** (duplicated + cut meshes inflate vertex counts and fight the LOD selection system — simplify decals heavily); each LOD should halve vertices at least and reduce texture memory + draw calls. **LODs:** at least 4 LODs, 2–3 only for tiny/simple props; tweak LODs in the in-sim **"high"** quality setting (neutral LOD selection; 50% minSize switches at 50% screen size). Numeric 2024 LOD policy (max 7 LODs, screen-size vertex budgets, ≥50% per-step) is **not duplicated here** — see the related LOD-workflow entry. 2024 scenery: prefer **SimProp Containers** (many small parts with their own LODs) over merging everything into one giant model.

**Incidental official rules (same docs, quick list):** animation bone affect limit = **4**; minimize skinned meshes (heavy CPU/memory), remove them as LODs allow; remove unused animations; when a skinned mesh's bones move elsewhere in the hierarchy the culling bounding box can desync (keep the skinned node in the moved hierarchy); tangents are computed at import — smooth surface, no overlapping verts in position/UV space, skinned tangents from the T-pose (start animations at frame 1+); all LODs need lights (avoid pop-in); collisions should prefer primitive shapes (rectangle/cylinder/sphere) over collidable materials.

entries.title: Alpha & transparency flicker — alphaMode=BLEND bug + glass-on-glass in 2024
entries.claim:
- DevSupport report (Jun 2024, exporter 3.3.1 on Blender 4.2): export always defaulted to `"alphaMode": "BLEND"` regardless of the shader setup (`gather_alpha_info` in `gltf2_blender_search_node_tree.py` falls through to BLEND) → flickering in the MSFS engine (materials blending with background textures). entries.title: Alpha Cutoff / clip threshold — an MSFS2024 addon material property, not a shader node: exports as JSON alphaCutoff, MASK-only, no viewport effect; channel workaround: feed alpha from Blend Alpha Map
entries.claim:
Channel episode (12–13/05/2024 — losconosciuto + mamu82): the **Alpha Cutoff (clip threshold)** slider "non mi cambia nulla" — no visible change however it was set; inspecting the exporter node tree between the texture input and the BSDF there is only a switch/mix node (blend mode changeable, **no adjustable cutoff value**); poster recalled a 0–1 range control existing once ("mi pare una volta ci fosse, con range 0-1"); enabling Clip in the plugin **does open the option** ("se abiliti il Clip ti si apre l'opzione"); the exported glTF **carries the values correctly** ("i valori tornano"). Suspicion voiced: "puzza quasi come se mancasse effettivamente un nodo al tree" — a node seems missing. Workaround that worked in the channel: disconnect **Base Color Multiplier A from Alpha** and connect the **Blend Alpha Map** instead ("funziona"). Use case context: fences/railings and nets ("ringhiere e reti") — alpha clip preferred for GPU efficiency (mamu82).

**SDK mechanic (2024 addon, fact cited):** Alpha Cutoff is **not a shader node — it never was** in the 2024 addon. It is a **material FloatProperty** `msfs_alpha_cutoff` (default 0.5: `ALPHACUTOFF = "Alpha Cutoff", 0.5, "msfs_alpha_cutoff", None` — `blender/utils/msfs_material_utils.py:67`), registered on materials with the description: *"When alpha mode is set to MASK the alphaCutoff property specifies the cutoff threshold. If the alpha value is greater than or equal to the alphaCutoff value … Alpha cutoff value is ignored for other modes"* (`io/com/extensions/material/asobo_material_common.py:502-511`), and **exported into the material JSON as `alphaCutoff`** (`asobo_material_common.py:179-183`; import-side read-back 328-330). The UI draws it **only when Alpha Mode = MASK** (`draw_alpha_cutoff_prop`, `blender/utils/msfs_material_utils.py:688-705`) — matching "se abiliti il Clip ti si apre l'opzione". In the node tree, MASK mode only toggles input 4 of the material's **Alpha Group** node (`_update_alpha_mode`, `blender/material/msfs_material.py:309-320`); the alpha source is selected by a blend switch node (texture output / vertex color / blend linear step; `msfs_material.py:1266-1300`). The **Blend Alpha Map** slot the channel rewired to is the in-tree "Detail alpha operator" node (`msfs_material.py:1562-1565, 1658`).

**Consequences (inferred, labeled):** (1) the cutoff is consumed by the **engine at runtime** from the material JSON — there is *no* viewport representation, so "nothing changes in Blender" when dragging the slider is **expected behavior, not a missing node**. (2) In the buggy exporter era that defaulted `alphaMode` to `BLEND` regardless of setup (entry `6f8372a1` — related; DevSupport report dated Jun 2024, 3.3.1 on Blender 4.2), the cutoff was silently inert in-engine because *"Alpha cutoff value is ignored for other modes"* — the May 2024 channel complaint predates that fix and is consistent with it. (3) The remembered 0–1 node matches the **2020-era** material pipeline (3ds Max Materials docs documented a Cutoff Threshold parameter); the 2024 FlightSim Material Parameters docs list no cutoff parameter for Standard (its only extra parameter is Pearl) — the 2024 cutoff exists addon-side only.

entries.title: Double-sided glass flicker — 2020 toolchain forced doubleSided on (glTF hand-edit fix); double-glazing recipe; 2024 addon has native Double Sided (default off)
entries.claim:
Channel exchange (ri-creativity, 12/09/2021, MSFS2020-era — robychiarta's pinned recipe): transparent glass that **flickers in the sun** — the exported/compiled material often had **`doubleSided` forced on** ("Tante volte devi togliere il double size manualmente perché lo mette sempre attivo" — often you must remove double-sided manually because it is always set active), even when the author had the checkbox off. Fix used in the channel: **open the exported glTF in a text editor (Notepad++) and set `doubleSided` to 0** per material. For true double glazing (two glass panes), the recipe is: duplicate the window mesh, **flip the second copy's normals**, and nudge it slightly inward ("la fai rientrare un pelo verso l'interno") — two single-sided panes visible from both sides via the pair, avoiding doubleSided entirely.

Caveat recorded in the same exchange (losconosciuto): with two *real* glass panes ~1 m apart, flicker **persisted even with doubleSided off** — one pane invisible when viewed from between them (loom video). DoubleSided alone was not the whole story in 2020: overlapping transparent surfaces (double panes / glass-on-glass) flicker regardless — matching the sorting-by-mesh-center mechanic documented in the alpha-flicker entry (related).

2024 pipeline (SDK-verified): the Blender addon has a **native Double Sided toggle, default OFF** (`DOUBLESIDED = "Double Sided", False, "msfs_double_sided"` — `blender/utils/msfs_material_utils.py:79`), mirrored onto Blender's `use_backface_culling` (`blender/material/msfs_material.py:1115`) and **exported as a material JSON property** (`io/com/extensions/material/asobo_material_common.py:189, 335, 516-521`; the FlipBackFaceNormal extension reads the same flag — `asobo_material_flip_back_face.py:39,53`). The NP++/manual glTF edit of the 2021 workaround is obsolete on the modern pipeline — the toggle goes through officially. (Whether the 2024 native compiler can still re-inject doubleSided like the 2020-era toolchain did is unverified.)

Community footprint for the phenomenon: DevSupport topic 3697 "Glass through the windshield? flickers, looks strange" (glass vs windshield material flicker) and FSDeveloper thread 460852 (2020 flickering transparency through models). The exact 'always-on doubleSided' exporter behavior has no corroboration outside the channel — labeled as such.

entries.title: MSFS 2024 rain on materials: `Receive Rain` opt-in — Windshield / Clearcoat only (standard and glass stay dry)
entries.claim:
Rain droplets in MSFS 2024 are opt-in per material: a surface only shows rain when its material has `Receive Rain` enabled (`msfs_receive_rain`, default OFF in the Blender addon) — with it off, no rain renders at all.

- Material-panel scope (2024 Blender addon, local SDK): the `Receive Rain` + `Rain Drop Tiling` UI is exposed only on the **Windshield** and **Clearcoat** material panels (`blender\material\msfs_material_windshield.py` line 237, `blender\material\msfs_material_clearcoat.py` line 377 — `draw_receive_rain_prop` is called there only). The exporter emits the glTF extension `ASOBO_material_rain_options` only when `msfs_receive_rain` is on (`io\com\extensions\material\asobo_material_rain_options.py`); schema: "This extension is used to add Rain on the surface material" with `rainDropScale` and `rainDropSide` ("For WindShield only", default false = front face).
- Official docs (Rain Effects — Windshield And Windows page): "Unlike previous versions of the simulation, in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 you do not need to set up specific UV's to handle the rain, as it is now all handled by a shader in the simulation automatically. However you still need to enable this shader using the Receive Rain parameter in the Windshield material options." Cockpit/cabin glass additionally needs **Rain On Backface** ("will invert the vertex position in the shader for spawning the rain"); a DevMode → Options debug "Windshield Rain" toggle exists to test the effect in-sim.
- Channel test on **scenery** (ri-creativity, 21-22/01/2025): no droplets on the MSFS **standard** material nor on the **glass** material of scenery objects; only a surface using a **Windshield**-type material showed them — and the effect is subtle: droplets visible only very close to the surface even at ultra settings (614nlv; losconosciuto: "solo il windshield fa le goccioline. Il glass nope").
- Community corroboration (avsim, Nov 2024): default-aircraft rain/wipers look weak; Fenix A32X dev FNX_Dave — the 2024 wiper system is "simply the one described in the SDK" (implemented in ~15-20 min; at launch only the AS350 used it among defaults).

entries.title: Mixamo FBX import — fix the location animation after applying the 0.01 scale
entries.claim:
Mixamo rigs import with the armature object scaled to `0.01` (Mixamo works in centimetres; the importer keeps the unit conversion on the object instead of rewriting bone/keyframe values). Applying Rotation & Scale to get an identity transform leaves the rotation keys correct but the location keys in the old units, so the hips (master) bone ends up ~100× out and the character drifts.

Procedure (fix the location F-curves):

1. Import the Mixamo rig / animation. Note the scale it comes in at — usually `0.01`, but always confirm (N-panel → Item → Scale).
2. Apply rotation and scale (`Ctrl+A` → Apply → Rotation & Scale).
3. Open the Graph Editor. Set the 2D cursor to frame 0, and the pivot to 2D Cursor Relative (top-right of the Graph Editor — the same control as the 3D View pivot menu).
4. Pose Mode → select all bones; in the Graph Editor filter box type `Location`.
5. Scale the location keys on the Y axis (in the Graph Editor, Y = the value axis), confirm, then set the operator's Y value to the original scale you noted (e.g. `0.01`) and confirm. (Keyboard path: `S`, `Y`, `0.01`, `Enter`, pointer over the Graph Editor.)

For FK-only rigs like Mixamo only the hips/master bone location curves actually matter (the rest are rotation-driven), so "select all + filter Location" is safe.

Notes (`fact (cited)` unless marked otherwise):

- Root cause: applying the object scale changes the skeleton↔unit ratio by 100× without touching the stored location values (Blender SE Q309202).
- Alternative: don't apply the scale at all — leave the armature at `0.01` (engines handle it); only bake it in if you do it consistently to every armature in the file, else clips "fly" 100× (Cinevva 2026).
- Some authors set the scene to Metric / Unit Scale `0.01` / Length `cm` before importing from Mixamo to avoid the mismatch (dev.btro.jp, 2025-07-09).
- Mixamo bones import in Quaternion rotation mode (Blender defaults to XYZ Euler) — relevant when hand-keying on top of a clip (jMonkeyEngine wiki).
- MSFS relevance: fix the location curves before the glTF export, or the exported clip carries the wrong translation and drifts in-sim. (inferred)

entries.title: Cascadeur animations — importing into Blender and the MSFS-compliant glTF export
entries.claim:
Import (Cascadeur → Blender). Cascadeur cannot emit glTF; export FBX (`File → Export → Export FBX/DAE`, preset Scene = model+animation or Animation = motion+skeleton only), with `Type fbx ascii` = Binary. In Blender use `File → Import → FBX` with defaults, but do NOT enable "Automatic Bone Orientation" (it corrupts the joints' rotations → broken animation). Collada is deprecated since Blender 4.5. Cascadeur uses centimetres, Blender metres (a Blender scale-1 model arrives at 100 in Cascadeur); Cascadeur's own advice to avoid scale/rotation drift is `Blender → target engine → Cascadeur → target engine`. If bones ignore the animation after applying the action, check each bone's Rotation mode in Pose Mode (Euler vs Quaternion). Cascadeur stores data on every frame, so curves arrive already dense/baked.

- Negative keyframes are rejected — the sim does not support them and the plugin errors on export; set `Negative Frames = Slide` or `Crop`.
- Bake constraints/drivers/IK with `Bake All Objects Animations`.

- `Reset pose bones between actions` (default on) when clips do not key every bone; `Set all glTF Animation starting at 0` for loops.
- For SimObjects also: `Use Asobo Unique ID Extension` + `Remove LOD Prefix`
+ `Generate TextureLib` + `Optimise Animation Size`.

entries.title: Parallax Window material — fake "behind glass" interiors (Blender workflow)
entries.claim:
The Parallax Window FlightSim material renders a fake interior behind window geometry with a parallax shader + a special texture layout — no interior geometry needed. In MSFS 2024 it's a dedicated material type (Blender panel material type `msfs_parallax_window`; glTF extension `ASOBO_material_parallax_window`) and the successor of the older 2020-era parallax tricks. It can be applied to any surface (building / airport / porthole windows).

How it works: the shader tiles the fake rooms using the second UV set (`UVMap2` in Blender, `UV2` in 3ds Max); Room Scale X/Y act on that UV set, so the fake-room layout is only as good as the UVMap2.

Texture slots (ParallaxWindow set, in order): Base Color (Front Glass Color) · Occlusion(R) Roughness(G) Metallic(B) · Normal (Front Glass Normal) · Emissive Ins Window (RGB) offset Time (A) · Behind Glass Color (RGB) Alpha (A) · Occlusion (UV2).

Room-grid rule (critical): Emissive Ins Window and Behind Glass Color must each be subdivided into a grid matching Room Count, each cell holding one room image sized relative to the cell's UV as: vertically floor 1/4, roof 1/2, walls 1/4; horizontally left wall 1/4, back wall 1/2, right wall 1/4. "Behind Glass Color (RGB) A" = interior albedo, "Emissive Ins Window (RGB) A" = interior emissive — both respect the same grid.

Parallax parameters (Blender panel):

- Room Scale X / Y — multiplier on the UVMap2 size of the fake room (horizontal / vertical); Room Scale Z — depth multiplier of the fake rooms.
- Room Count — number of rooms available on the two grid textures.
- Corridor — toggle: left/right walls are not rendered → rooms connect on the horizontal axis → corridor look from an angle.

Blender addon specifics (SDK source): Alpha mode forced to `MASK` (`msfs_material_parallax.py:87-89`); defaults Room Scale X/Y/Z = 0.5/0.5/0.5, Room Count = 5, Corridor = off (`blender\utils\msfs_material_utils.py:157-162`); material type `msfs_parallax_window` (`io\com\extensions\material\asobo_material_common.py:358`); extension/export `ASOBO_material_parallax_window` (`asobo_material_parallax_window.py`); glTF schema: `parallaxScale`, `roomSizeXScale`, `roomSizeYScale`, `roomNumberXY`, `behindWindowMapTexture` (`Schemas\ASOBO_material_parallax_window\gltf.ASOBO_material_parallax_window.schema.json`). Shader techs: `Tech_Parallax` / `Tech_Parallax_TwoSide` (`Fx\MSFS2024Material_ParallaxWindow.fx`). Parallax Window excluded from detail-map slots (no detail maps, 3ds Max UI).

Porthole material (same trick, aircraft): albedo alpha encodes depth — glass 0.8–1, frame 0.5–0.75, invisible 0; normals only on the frame exterior, never the interior (else applied to the glass); emissive = interior projection, tileable horizontally, opposing windows at alpha 0 (becomes transparent and receives global lighting); mesh normals must be oriented horizontally (e.g. Edit Normals); the effect degrades at extreme angles — keep albedo alpha consistent and set occlusion (R) white on the exterior side of the window.

entries.title: MSFS material tinting — Color Multiplier / vertex colors need white albedo; 2024 addon mixes Vertex Color into the exported shader (no stock preview)
entries.claim:
Channel exchange (ri-creativity, 20/12/2024): to re-tint a *textured* material to white (hangar interior: green outside, white inside), changing the material's **Albedo Color / Base Color leaves the original texture color untouched** ("se cambio l'Albedo Color, su bianco mi tiene il colore originale" — the albedo texture's own colors win). Community answers: the **Color Multiplier** control of the MSFS standard material is the intended tint parameter; otherwise use **vertex colors** (mamu82). Chain rule derived in the channel: **tinting (Color Multiplier or vertex colors) multiplies the albedo texture, so it needs a white / near-white albedo to be effective** — a colored albedo resists the tint; re-coloring therefore needs white albedo + tint rather than tint alone, and detail preservation is a concern (losconosciuto — "non deve perdere il dettaglio della texture").

SDK mechanics (2024 Blender addon):
- The material node tree **wires a Vertex Color node into the exported shader** — vertex color is mixed into the exporter nodes (`blender/material/msfs_material.py` ~line 1187 `vertex_color_map_node`, feeding detail-blend / blend_linear_step / blend_switch inputs).
- The addon **auto-creates a default vertex color layer on new or converted meshes** (curve-to-mesh etc.) so that shader node always has data (`blender/msfs_handlers.py:26-28`).
- Exporter: `export_vertex_color`, `export_all_vertex_colors`, `export_active_vertex_color_when_no_material` settings; at export the active color attribute is renamed to the default name and its domain/type enforced (`io/exp/multi_export.py:340-342, 708-725`).
- The 2024 addon property list has **Base Color** factor (`msfs_base_color_factor`, `blender/utils/msfs_material_utils.py:60`) but **no literal "Color Multiplier" property** — Color Multiplier belongs to the 2020-era standard-material pipeline; the 2024 docs document no Color Multiplier for Standard (Pearl is its only additional parameter).

Channel culture (same channel, 2020-era dates): repeated advice "never export with vertex coloring" — TexTools / similar could inject vertex paint and break ID bakes, so meshes were exported with Vertex Colors unchecked under Geometry (declog lines 3915, 4125, 6261-6270). The 2024 addon's explicit vertex-color handling supersedes that workflow.

entries.title: Renaming an exported glTF breaks the build — internal `.bin` buffer reference keeps the old name (`tinygltf: File not found`); re-point the JSON URI or export with final names
entries.claim:
Channel episode (ri-creativity, 21/05/2021, MSFS2020-era — losconosciuto + robychiarta): renaming exported files breaks the build. The exported `.gltf` **embeds the buffer reference to its `.bin` by name** ("quando esporti, ti crea la dipendenza nel GLTF"); rename the `.gltf`/`.bin` afterwards and the compiler fails with `tinygltf: File not found : <old name>.bin` — the internal JSON buffer URI still points at the original name ("se il riferimento è a LFBP Airconditioner.bin, e io lo rinomino… non lo troverà mai"). Fix used in the channel: open the glTF in a text editor and **re-point the buffer URI** to the renamed `.bin` ("sono entrato nei GLTF ed ho richiamato i file .bin giusti"). Exporting with the final names from the start avoids the whole class.

Community footprint (same mechanic): FSDeveloper thread "MSFS20 — Can't find 'bin' file" ("make sure that the glTF file does actually reference that bin file and not another one"); DevSupport topic 3388 "Multiple GLTFs with one BIN = compiler error" — the compiler resolves the `.bin` reference strictly, so one shared BIN across several glTFs errors too.

2024 pipeline (SDK): the exporter derives the `.bin` path from the export path (`io/exp/multi_export.py:1251` — `bin_path = bpy.path.ensure_ext(export_path, ".bin")`), so files exported with final names (LOD Groups / `[MODEL]_LODn.gltf`) carry matching internal references automatically. Renaming after export breaks identically; re-pointing the JSON URI still works as the manual fix.

Related context from the same episode (kept as note, not merged): the 2020 exporter also failed outright when exporting LODs together with animations — stripping animations/NLA tracks, exporting LODs, then re-adding animations and exporting one-by-one was the working routine; XML naming was manual (`<LOD ModelFile="…_LOD00.gltf" minSize="8"/>`).

entries.title: Substance Painter bake artifacts — `Average Normal` flag (Normal Tangent baker, default ON) breaks AO / curvature / thickness
entries.claim:
Community report (ri-creativity channel, 20-21/01/2025): AO bakes in Substance Painter kept producing artifacts — surviving radius tuning, triangulated-FBX export and flat-shaded geometry — until the culprit was toggled off: the **Average Normal** option, **on by default**, on the **Normal Tangent** baker. With it enabled, artifacts hit the **AO** map mainly, plus **curvature** and **thickness**; disabling it cleans all three (re-enabling brings the artifacts straight back, even when baking only AO).

- Second-poster diagnosis: the flag belongs to the normal/tangent computation, not the AO baker — "il fatto che sballasse l'AO era una conseguenza di un problema con il calcolo dei tangent" — so the AO artifacts are a downstream symptom of the tangent calculation; mesh problems (bad normals, hidden geometry) can trip it.
- Checklist before blaming the AO baker (same thread): bake AO on an **exploded copy** of the model, never on the whole assembled model ("Le AO andrebbero fatte sugli esplosi — mai sul modello intero") — bake on the exploded copy, apply on the non-exploded original; re-inspect the mesh for **hidden faces** in edit mode; **merge duplicate vertices** (poster: always merge at 1 mm).
- Independent corroboration (reddit r/Substance3D, baking high-poly → low-poly): "most importantly the Average Normals option ticked off (it's on by default. Weird artifacts when baking high poly onto low poly)".
- MSFS context: the official cockpit-texturing docs cover AO baking (Arnold lightmap vs Substance Painter AO comparison — Ambient Occlusion page); community SP↔MSFS export/material templates exist (github.com/synapticsim/Substance-MSFS: Standard / Anisotropy / Clear Coat / Windshield). Adobe helpx baking docs were unreachable during verification (HTTP 403) — the flag's canonical wording and default-on status rest on the two independent community reports above.

entries.title: CGL aerial scenery for MSFS 2024 — QGIS XYZ tiles to Bing quadkey PNGs (Tiles2Bing gone; Python replacement + build workflow)
entries.claim:
CGL aerial scenery pipeline for MSFS 2024 (deep-dive research, source C, 2026-09-24): QGIS XYZ tiles → Bing-quadkey-named PNGs → CGL package. Verified against the official 2024 docs, the shipped SimpleAerial sample and the community toolchain.

1. Official CGL background. CGL files are "container files used by the simulation to hold compressed imagery, elevation, and/or vector data about the world", stored "following a quadtree scheme, based on a mercator projection" — i.e. the Bing Maps Tile System; CGL is "the Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 equivalent of BGL files", but "at the moment this data cannot be edited by add-ons" except the imagery route. Add-on aerials: "you can modify the simulation CGL images used for terrain... create a number of PNG format images (named with the quadtree key to identify the location where they are to be used) and then use the CGL Asset Type in the Project Editor". The XML lives next to the images folder (the shipped sample puts it at `PackageSources\CGL\CGLBuilderConfig.xml` — the docs' "vegetation folder" wording does not match the sample):

    <CGLBuilder>
    	<CGL type="SecondaryAerialImage" input="Tiles" directory="aerial_images"/>
    </CGLBuilder>

    `type` (only "SecondaryAerialImage" for custom aerials), `input` (only "Tiles" — each file is one tile whose NAME IS THE QUADKEY of the tile, with a `*.png` extension), `directory` (sub-folder relative to the XML).

2. Authoring specs (CGL Files page). Aerial PNGs are authored at LOD20 — map width/height 268,435,456 px, ground resolution 0.1493 m/pixel, "16bit PNG", fixed 256x256 px; "the build process will automatically generate the images for the lower levels of detail as part of the generated CGL file". The PNG ALPHA blends with the in-game aerial: alpha 0 = in-game aerial pixel, alpha 1 = your pixel, in-between = linear interpolation (use it to feather the edges of the override area).

3. Step 1 — QGIS tile extraction (verified routes):
- Browser panel → right-click "XYZ Tiles" → New Connection with the Bing aerial URL `http://ecn.t3.tiles.virtualearth.net/tiles/a{q}.jpeg?g=1` (any XYZ/WMTS source works; Bing URL from the AW-MSFS tutorial); zoom to the target area.
- Processing Toolbox → Raster tools → "Generate XYZ tiles (Directory)" — set extent and zoom levels (~17–20), produces `z/x/y.png`.
- GeoTIFF route (community-favoured): export your composited raster EPSG:3857, cut with GTiff2Tiles (`GTiff2Tiles.Console.exe --input test.tif --output Tiles --minz 20 --maxz 20 --tms FALSE -c mercator` — github.com/Gigas002/GTiff2Tiles) or `gdal2tiles.py --xyz -z 17-20`; "EPSG:3857 for both geotiff and tiles" gives metres/pixel units (rhumbaflappy).

4. Step 2 — XYZ → Bing quadkey conversion and the Tiles2Bing situation:
- The original `tiles2bing` (Christine Winther, v0.0.2) was a small .NET-Core CLI: `tiles2bing "\path\to\Tiles" /o "\path\to\PackageSources\CGL\aerial_images" /y google` — `/y google` = input uses the standard XYZ (top-left) y-axis. Its official distribution is GONE (May 2025: "it seems the tiles2bing tool is no longer available"). Surviving copies are community-shared: rhumbaflappy's fixed build (FSDeveloper threads 457437 / 448680 — framework-dependent .NET app; keep the matching runtimes installed, the newest-only install breaks it: "dotnet chooses the one it needs... I think that might be your problem"), a OneDrive mirror (thread 458692), and the Sep-2026 "AerialWorkshop" bundle (GeotiffCreator + GTiff2Tiles + tiles2bing + a batch file producing the aerial_images folder, FSDeveloper 461140).
- Python-replacement feasibility: HIGH and trivial — the conversion is a pure RENAME to quadkey names. XYZ tiles from QGIS/GTiff2Tiles/GDAL sit on the same Web-Mercator global grid as Bing tiles (2^z × 2^z, origin top-left) at the same zoom, so NO resampling is needed: for each tile compute `quadkey` from (x, y, z) — for i = z..1 take bit (i−1) of x and y: digit = (X bit) + 2·(Y bit), append as base-4 digit; quadkey length = z (official algorithm + full C# reference in the Bing Maps Tile System article). TMS-flipped input needs y′ = 2^z − 1 − y first. A ~40-60 line Pillow script walks the XYZ dir → writes `<quadkey>.png` (force 256x256, RGBA, alpha feathering) → emits CGLBuilderConfig.xml + a SimpleAerial-style project XML. Only dependency: Pillow. Tiles2Bing's disappearance is therefore NOT a blocker.

5. Step 3 — package build (official sample pattern, SDK `Samples\DevmodeProjects\Sceneries\SimpleAerial\`):
- `SimpleAerialProject.xml` (Project Version="2", FolderName="Packages", `<Package>` → `PackageDefinitions\mycompany-aerial.xml`); `PackageSources\CGL\CGLBuilderConfig.xml` as in §1; `PackageSources\CGL\aerial_images\` containing the quadkey PNGs (the shipped tiles are 20-digit quadkeys = LOD20).
- DevMode → File → Open project… → `SimpleAerial.xml` → Project Editor → right-click the project → Build and Mount → package in `Packages\mycompany-aerial`, mounted in the VFS; sample teleport test: lat 47.000744, lon -122.858906 (the sim caches the area — teleport far away first if already positioned there).

6. Empirical notes (MSFS 2024 runtime, community-verified): pre-SU3, LOD19 tiles did not show and LOD20 needed a TIN-exclude polygon; SU3 fixed the bleed-through — "the aerial CGL just works" without exclusions (FSDeveloper 448680, p10, 2025). rhumbaflappy's iteration loop uses LOD17-18 for colour tests (2-4 h speed) and LOD20 for the final compile; a full 5-minute round trip is typical with the GTiff2Tiles + tiles2bing batch.

7. Projection — EPSG:3857 ONLY. The CGL quadtree lives on the spherical Web-Mercator plane (Bing Maps Tile System): zoom z = a global 2^z × 2^z grid of 256×256 px tiles, origin top-left, latitude clip ±85.05112878°, tile boundaries on EPSG:3857 (pseudo-Mercator) coordinates — not on lat/lon degrees, UTM or any local CRS. So every source must be reprojected to EPSG:3857 (set QGIS project CRS + raster CRS to EPSG:3857) and the composite GeoTIFF exported in EPSG:3857 BEFORE XYZ-tiling; tiles cut from a 4326/UTM 32632/3003/23032 mosaic will not match the quadkey grid and the CGL lands misaligned. The Piemonte ombreggiature WMS already serves EPSG:3857 natively (verified capabilities) → request the hillshade in 3857 directly. Ground resolution in 3857 = 156543.03392 / 2^z m/px × cos(latitude) (Bing article; z20 = 0.1493 m/px at the equator); at Domodossola (~46.1° N) z20 resolves ~0.1036 m/px — size your source imagery so it samples at or above the zoom you compile.

8. Georeferencing through Photoshop (or GIMP/Affinity). They all STRIP the internal GeoTIFF tags on save — 'Photoshop gets rid of the metadata that makes it a GeoTIFF' (GIS StackExchange 423985); paint.net is the exception (preserves GeoTIFF attributes — why rhumbaflappy's CGL colour loop uses it, thread 454878). The robust fix is a world-file sidecar: export the stitched GeoTIFF with `.tfw` (QGIS Raster → Conversion → Translate → advanced parameter `tfw` = `yes`; or `gdal_translate -co TFW=YES -co PROFILE=BASELINE in.tif out.tif` — BASELINE drops internal geo tags so the world file becomes the ONLY georef source). A world file is 6 plain-text lines: pixel X size, rotation Y (0), rotation X (0), pixel Y size (negative), X/Y of the top-left PIXEL CENTER (GDAL WLD driver); PS never touches it. Then: (a) edit in PS keeping the exact pixel grid — NO crop/resize/rotation or the world file is invalid; (b) Save As TIFF keeping alpha ('Save Transparency'; the alpha channel is what CGL uses to blend with the in-game aerial, so paint your border feathering into it); (c) reload in QGIS (it reads the sidecar) and check alignment against the Bing XYZ layer — a few-metre offset between independent sources is the norm; fix by re-georeferencing (QGIS Georeferencer, Linear) or hand-editing the 6 .tfw numbers. If you must crop, do it in QGIS BEFORE PS (Raster → Extraction → Clip) or re-georeference after — never blind-crop in PS. Validate the alpha survives the tiling step on the first batch (one check tile under QGIS/GTiff2Tiles: the CGL blend depends on it).

entries.title: Custom elevation for terrain — 5m DEM vs default MSFS 2024 mesh (hillshade compositing instead of mesh injection)
entries.claim:
The 5 m elevations for Domodossola (Piemonte LIDAR-era data) versus the default MSFS 2024 terrain — deep-dive research, source C, 2026-09-24. Answer: the 5 m DEM is finer than the default mesh in principle, but MSFS 2024 exposes NO add-on path to inject custom elevation into the terrain — so the DEM's productive role is generating HILLSHADE that is composited into the CGL aerial imagery, not replacing the mesh.

1. 2020 and 2024 SHARE the same height field. Jorg Neumann (WU XVII announcement, 24 Jul 2024): "We are not going to have two different digital twins — cities like London are going to be shared, POIs are shared, the height field (DEM) and aerials are all shared. What's different in MSFS 2024 is we have optimized how the data is brought to the player." So 2024 did not ship a new global DEM — it changed streaming, not data.

2. What the default data actually is. An EU data-policy change let Asobo use "incredibly accurate digital elevation maps... closer to one to two meters" (vs ~20-30 m before) — but only for regions re-mapped by world updates (flagship: WU XVII Great Britain, with LiDAR DEM + TIN surface modeling). Elsewhere the community-decompiled default 2024 mesh (FSDeveloper 460737, Mar 2026) is an "Enhanced Terrain Mesh" at ~10 m horizontal spacing built from Sentinel-1 SAR DEM/DTM: each ~10x10 m cell becomes a triangulated irregular network (TIN) with linear interpolation between vertices — smooth but unable to represent anything under ~10 m (micro-relief, narrow embankments, ditches), with SAR altimetric noise; SDK DevMode lets you inspect the live mesh structure.

3. Alps status (as of 2026-09-24). No dedicated Alpine TIN/DEM world update has shipped: the first "country-side TIN" world update was WU22 US National Parks (Jul 2026), and the community wishlist explicitly asks "I'm hoping for the Alps next (DACH+Italy+France)". Domodossola therefore sits on the generic ~10 m SAR-based mesh — a 5 m DEM is meaningfully finer, but see §4.

4. You CANNOT feed it to the mesh. CGL files store elevation data, but "at the moment this data cannot be edited by add-ons" (SDK intro; "in the future it may be possible"); the SDK DEM doc page is a TO-DO stub; the ONLY add-on CGL asset type is `SecondaryAerialImage` (imagery — see the CGL pipeline entry). There is no add-on custom-mesh / custom-elevation API in 2024; airport polygons/aprons only flatten or adjust around the default mesh (see the ground-displacement entry: do not confuse DEM heightmaps with ground-material displacement — different system).

5. What the 5 m DEM IS for: (a) the "Satellite AND elevation" branch = generate a shaded relief and composite it with the satellite imagery BEFORE tiling (QGIS: Raster → Terrain Analysis → Hillshade, or GDAL `gdaldem hillshade`; sun azimuth/altitude under your control) — the CGL aerial then carries realistic relief shading over the default 10 m mesh, which is the practical maximum visual gain; (b) geometry QA (runway slopes, airport flatten checks).

6. Ready-made hillshade: the Piemonte geoportal already serves it — `https://geomap.reteunitaria.piemonte.it/WEBCAT/CAPABILITIES/wms_regp_ombreggiature.xml` is a LIVE WMS 1.1.1 capabilities (mapproxy, CSI Piemonte): layer `regp_ombreggiature`, title "Ripresa Aerea ICE 2009-2011 - Rilievo ombreggiato" (hillshade of the ICE 2009-2011 aerial survey), GetMap png/jpeg, SRS EPSG:3857 (also 4326/32632/3003/23032), bbox ~4.8-11.1 E / 43.8-46.6 N. In QGIS: Layer → Add Layer → Add WMS/WMTS Layer with the capabilities URL, pick the ombreggiature layer, set Multiply/Overlay blending under the satellite source, then run the tile generation over the composite. Expect a few-metre misalignment between independent sources (community norm) — verify against the Bing layer in QGIS first.

Verdict for Domodossola: implement Satellite AND hillshade (from the 5 m DEM or the ombreggiature WMS); do not chase mesh replacement — the default ~10 m SAR mesh (un-upgraded region) + 5 m-derived shading texture is the practical maximum for CGL aerial scenery today.

entries.title: Projected Mesh objects — independent placement outside airports
entries.claim:
A Projected Mesh renders a scenery model projected flat onto terrain (2D) instead of in 3D — used in airports to add terrain detail.

- Independent placement (2024): "By default, Projected Mesh objects require one or more Airport Objects to be present in the scene… If no airport is present and you still require a Projected Mesh, then you should check the box labelled Independent Object before adding it to the scene" — the group is then created in the scenery root instead of inside an airport group. (This confirms the community technique for non-airport areas; fs-sdk channel, mamu82, 15/05/2024.)
- Overlap & draw order: overlapping meshes must have different priorities (higher = rendered over lower; same-priority order is not guaranteed). Draw Before slots the mesh into the render hierarchy (e.g. before MARKINGS → over aprons/taxiways/runways, under markings/marking text). Placed outside the airport Object Test Radius → not rendered.
- Rendering: meshes are baked into the terrain textures (polycount savings, terraformable) — quality capped by terrain resolution (~4mm/px at the equator; best LODs reserved for airports; increases with the "Terrain level of detail" setting). The source object itself is not required in the final package (baked into the glTF).
- Authoring constraints: export models without translation/rotation/ scale (transforms are dropped — use the Scenery Editor Gizmo instead); only albedo, metal-rough-AO, normal maps + detail counterparts are allowed — metal and AO components are not used. Ground Merging blends terrain with the material textures; Surface Type has no visual effect (choose it for correct VFX/audio); snow coverage is automatic (darker areas less snow; asphalt/cement/paint materials and roads reduce it).

entries.title: Displacement / tessellation — ground-material-only, authored via Ground Surface heightmap settings
entries.claim:
Displaced / tessellated textures in MSFS2024 are a GROUND-material feature only: the engine generates displacement on terrain and ground surfaces (polygons / aprons / projected-mesh areas), and the developer-facing authoring lives in the Material Inspector's Ground Surface Settings — no 3D-model material exposes it.

- Authoring (Material Inspector, Ground Surface context): supply a greyscale heightmap texture, then set `Heightmap Range` (maps pure white→pure black to a height range in centimeters), `Heightmap Blend Below Threshold` (alpha threshold for the "hollows") and `Heightmap Blend Above Threshold` (alpha threshold for the "bumps"). The three settings are only visible once a heightmap texture is supplied. Release notes frame them as "ground material heightmaps".
- Engine-generated on terrain: the displacement is generated for the ground by the engine — developers have no direct SDK control over it (DevSupport feature request open); the user-facing graphics option "Displacement Mapping" toggles this terrain relief.
- Do NOT confuse with rectangle heightmaps (DEMs) — a different system (DevSupport KB).
- Scope check: the full FlightSim material parameter list for 3D models has no displacement/tessellation/POM entry (see related entries).

DevSupport report (SDK / engine 1.0.77.0 era): displacement-map materials applied to polygons or aprons render correctly in the DevMode editor but NOT in the compiled package at runtime — "Displacement / Tessellation doesn't work in the game engine for terrain mesh".

Related KB discussion (topic 10433) shows the surrounding pain: terrain displacement is engine-generated and developers cannot suppress it through polygons and/or projected meshes (requested feature); meshes placed anywhere other than concrete or asphalt will engrave into the displaced ground.

No confirmed workaround and no confirmation that the bug is fixed in the current SDK (1.7.3, Sep 2026).
