entries.title: 2020→2024 project conversion — 2024 compiler hang at `Generating Package Information` (no error) / editor CTD; practice: port from 2020, don't convert
entries.claim:
Channel report (ri-creativity, 25/11/2024 — single-poster anecdote, personal scenery): converting an old 2020 airport project (Blackbushe) into the 2024 toolchain made the compiler **hang at `Generating Package Information`** with **no error output** — clean, rebuild and manual delete+rebuild all failed on the then-latest SDK. Second poster (mamu82): converting another old scenery did not crash the compiler, but the project **CTD'd once loaded in the 2024 DevMode editor**. Both concluded it was not worth converting old scenery.

- Workaround / prevailing community practice (multiple, independent): **don't convert — keep developing in the 2020 SDK and port/test against 2024**. FSDeveloper best-practice thread (Jun 2025): GaryGB — "It is more practical to develop in 2020 then 'port' to 2024" (workflow: load the original 2020 package into the 2024 Community folder for run-time comparison; copy the whole 2020 project, open its XML in the 2024 Scenery Editor, run a 2024 build and inspect the compiler Console log); WildLynxPilot — pure-2020 sceneries that "never saw the 2024 SDK" run fine in 2024 (serialized in a 2020-mode, no LOD popping); Nordscape — visuals differ between the sims (materials, light intensity), ending with two separate per-sim versions is pragmatic.
- Official-side framing: many 2020 packages need no conversion and run in 2024 unchanged (Asobo: "All projects should be compatible with 2024"); DevSupport advice for moving a 2020 project is to copy the project folder and open/convert it in the 2024 DevMode (topics 11708, 15388). Asobo shipped no dedicated DevMode "Project Converter" — the 2024 SDK's conversion helpers are 3ds Max-side scripts (`SceneConversion2024\MSFS2024_SceneConversion.ms:29` → `convertMSFS2020ObjectsToMSFS2024Object`); the `Generating Package Information` string is absent from SDK sources.
- Related DevMode failure class: scenery-editing CTDs in the 2024 DevMode are separately reported (devsupport topic 14090).

Honesty note (user-confirmed: "this was mostly my personal experience"): the exact hang message has no other community footprint — treat the compiler-hang symptom as a lone anecdote; the port-not-convert practice is the well-corroborated part.

entries.title: 3D model materials — no displacement/POM input; parallax = fake interiors, FakeTerrain = terrain shading
entries.claim:
3D-model FlightSim materials (scenery objects / SimObject meshes) expose NO displacement, tessellation or POM parameter — in MSFS2024 a material cannot displace model geometry. What exists on meshes instead:

- `ParallaxWindow` / `Porthole` material types — fake-interior parallax (UV2-driven room tiling / parallax scrolling), NOT depth displacement. Workflow detail in the Parallax Window entry (related).
- `FakeTerrain` material type — "The terrain material type. Meshes with this type will have the same shading system as the terrain in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024." The only documented route for a mesh to borrow ground/terrain shading.
- Confirmed by absence: the full FlightSim Materials parameter/texture list contains no displacement entry, and the SDK Blender add-on + glTF schemas define no displacement extension (0 grep hits for displacement/tessellation/POM across `Tools\Blender\addons`, `Schemas\`, `ModelBehaviorDefs\`).

entries.title: POM / SPOM are not MSFS SDK terms — official wording is displacement mapping / tessellation (ground) and parallax (fake interiors)
entries.claim:
The acronyms "POM" (Parallax Occlusion Mapping) and "SPOM" appear NOWHERE in the MSFS2024 official documentation, SDK sources, or DevSupport — they are not SDK terminology. When someone says "POM / displaced texture" in MSFS2024 they are (imprecisely) describing one of two official features:

- Ground materials: "displacement mapping" / "tessellation" — engine-generated terrain relief + Ground Surface heightmap settings (related entry).
- 3D models: "parallax" — the fake-interior `ParallaxWindow` / `Porthole` material types (related entry); no depth displacement exists there.

Verified by exhaustive case-insensitive greps: `Documentation\public` (*.md) for parallax occlusion|SPOM|POM|tessellat = 0 hits; SDK sources (`Tools\Blender\addons`, `Schemas\`, `ModelBehaviorDefs\`) = 0 hits; official docs + DevSupport sweep found no use of the terms.

entries.title: FakeTerrain material — properties, quirks and uses (terrain shading on custom meshes)
entries.claim:
FakeTerrain is "The terrain material type. Meshes with this type will have the same shading system as the terrain in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024" — the standard way to make a custom 3D mesh (helipads, aprons, ground scenery) adopt terrain-style lighting/shading. The identical wording existed in the MSFS2020 docs, so the type is not new to 2024.

Engine / SDK side:

- Dedicated glTF extension `ASOBO_material_fake_terrain` — bare on/off flag only: schema `gltf.ASOBO_material_fake_terrain.schema.json:7` (key `enabled`), exporter writes just `{"enabled": True}` (addon `io\com\extensions\material\asobo_material_fake_terrain.py:53-60`); docs: "Used to enable or disable the FakeTerrain material property".
- No material-specific parameters — docs list "Additional Parameters: N/A" (flightsim-materials index.md:223) and no FakeTerrain section exists in flightsim-material-parameters.
- Blender add-on: material type "Fake Terrain" (`msfs_fake_terrain`, panel dropdown asobo_material_common.py:363; enum msfs_material_utils.py:34), class `MSFS2024_Fake_Terrain` (msfs_material_fake_terrain.py:23). Property list (msfs_material_fake_terrain.py:25-68): Base Color, Emissive (Color/Scale/Day/Night multipliers), Draw Order Offset, No Cast Shadow, Two-Sided, Flip Backface Normal, Disable Motion Blur, Metal/Rough/Occlusion/Normal scales, Detail UV scale / Detail Normal scale / Detail Blend Threshold, UV offset/tiling/rotation/clamp, and Gameplay flags CollisionMaterial / RoadCollisionMaterial / GroundCollisionMaterial. NO alpha-mode control in its list or panels → base default ALPHAMODE = "OPAQUE" (msfs_material_utils.py:58).
- Textures: the shared Standard-group set — Base Color, Occlusion(R) Roughness(G) Metallic(B), Normal, Emissive, Detail Color/Detail ORM/Detail Normal (detail maps are compressed — cannot be reused in other slots), Blend Mask (`MTL_BITMAP_BLENDMASK`; Detail slots become Secondary Color/ORM), Occlusion (UV2) (flightsim-material-textures index.md:9-96; texture-xml-properties index.md:48).
- Decal compatibility (docs): "Decal materials will only be rendered over: Standard, ClearCoat, Anisotropic, FakeTerrain and SSS" (flightsim-materials index.md:110). Note the separate community claim that DevMode polygons/aprons/projected meshes cannot be layered OVER an imported custom 3D mesh — that is a DevMode-layering limitation, not a contradiction of material-level decal support.

Quirks (community-verified, MSFS2024):

- NO wet/rain/puddles effect: a Blender-mesh helipad with FakeTerrain "is not producing the wet effect like the default terrain" (FSDeveloper 460630, Jan-Feb 2026; OP's expected behavior contradicted by observation — no confirmed workaround yet; suggested untested: layered Terraforming Rectangles + flat mesh, or Projected Mesh instead).
- NO seamless blending with surrounding terrain: alpha blending / decals tried, best result albedo transparency with a "shadow" artifact in the transition zone (even with Do-not-cast-shadow).
- Lighting ≠ true terrain: "it certainly doesn't look 100% like terrain and always stands out at certain daytimes" (FSDeveloper 451768); it also gives NO collision — mesh needs a collision-tagged material, and runways/taxiways/markings render only on official terrain, not on FakeTerrain meshes.
- Alpha/mask quirk (tool-dependent): 3ds Max/MCX path keeps mask alpha (pre-select Mask mode in Standard, then switch type to FakeTerrain) — FSDeveloper 454079 "glass blending with Trees (SOLVED)"; the Blender add-on instead drops the alpha to opaque when switching to FakeTerrain (no alpha control in its panel).

Uses / examples: custom heliport ground mesh (FSDeveloper 460630); vegetation/tree alpha blending via Mask mode (FSDeveloper 454079); bridge/taxiway-over-water experiments using terrain lighting on a stand-in mesh (FSDeveloper 451768). Local SDK Samples ship NO FakeTerrain example (0 grep hits). DevMode Options has an unrelated debug "Fake Terrain" toggle (menus/options index.md:146).

entries.title: Placed Animal SimObject wander logic — automatic ground-AI wandering around spawn or itinerary-driven? (Bears sample documents placement, not movement)
entries.claim:
A placed Animal-category SimObject (Scenery Editor SimObj instance) has all movement equipment in sim.cfg — [contact_points] resting, [DesignSpecs] max_speed_mph + acceleration/deceleration, [WAYPOINT] CanReverse — and its animations.xml switches Walk↔Idle on (A:GROUND VELOCITY). Research 2026-09-23 (source C, 6cb28791 verification) established WHAT IS documented:

- **`[WAYPOINT]` controls AI movement BETWEEN points** (ai.cfg docs, `C:\MSFS 2024 SDK\Documentation\public\flighting\content-configuration\cfg-files\ai.cfg\index.md:48-61`): "This section controls how the AI will deal with taxiway points, specifically the way it will move between them" — SlowDownDistance (50.0 default), SlowDownSpeed (0.4 kts), StopDistance (2.0 m), SlowDownOnLastWayPoint (TRUE), CanReverse (TRUE default; the Bears sample sets 0), FrontRadiusMeters (-1.0 → bbox). So the ground AI CAN move a placed SimObject, but the docs only describe point-to-point movement tuning — they never say where a placed animal's POINTS come from or whether any are auto-generated around the spawn.
- **Human SimObjects get movement from XML waypoint navigation** (Ground Traffic docs, `...environment\living-world\ground-traffic\index.md:10-16`): idle workers'/marshallers' "behavior... is defined in their XML files (in the *AirportServices* folder), and it will describe the way the object navigates the waypoints used to move around, and its animations"; the marshaller "uses an AI simulation to set some SimVars" driving its animations. Analogous XML-driven navigation for animals is NOT documented.
- **Ambient vehicles move semi-randomly via TaxiPaths** (`ground-traffic\index.md:22-40`): vehicles wait random time, pick a random unoccupied parking, taxi there via `TaxiPaths` (VEHICLE type preferred, runways avoided, ATC-aware); a `RatioOfAmbientVehiclesThatAreImmobile` fraction never moves. This is the closest documented 'random roaming' analog — but it belongs to the Living World airport-traffic system, not to a Scenery-Editor-placed Animal.
- **No 'Itinerary' feature in the 2024 docs** — 2020's Scenery Editor itinerary mechanism has zero matches in the flighting docs; the 2024 placement flow (SimObj Objects → Add → gizmos/One-Click) has no itinerary/wander option.
- **Community datapoints:** default 2024 animals spawn as Living World entities (DevSupport 11803) and default fauna visibly moves/flees (World Photographer fauna reports — deer run away from low flight); FSDeveloper 'Does Living World Work?' (5394, 2007 — FSX-era third-party tool) is only tangential ('animals configured either like a vehicle... fish/whales comparable to boats'). Nothing found describes the behavior of a CUSTOM placed Animal SimObject — neither proof of automatic random wandering nor of full staticity.

Verdict: STILL OPEN. The ground-AI point-to-point machinery ([WAYPOINT]), the XML-waypoint navigation precedent (humans), and the semi-random TaxiPath roaming (ambient vehicles) all suggest placed animals COULD move without addon scripts, but no official sentence or community record confirms the trigger, radius or randomness of a solo placed animal's wandering. Needs an in-sim test (place the Bears sample animal, observe) or a DevSupport/FSDeveloper thread.

updated.note: Source-C verification run (user request): folded in ai.cfg [WAYPOINT] parameter semantics (point-to-point AI movement tuning), Ground Traffic XML-waypoint navigation precedent for human SimObjects, ambient-vehicle semi-random TaxiPath roaming as the nearest documented analog, the 2024 docs' zero 'Itinerary' matches, and community datapoints (DevSupport 11803 default Living-World spawn; World Photographer fauna flee reports; FSDeveloper 5394 FSX-era tangential). Question remains open — the wander trigger/radius for a solo placed Animal is still undocumented; an in-sim test of the Bears sample is the suggested next step.

rows.summary: Follow-up research amendment to Category 9 entry d32b62db ('CGL aerial scenery for MSFS 2024 — QGIS XYZ tiles to Bing quadkey PNGs...') — user asked (a) what projection to generate tiles in and (b) how to preserve georeferencing when editing the stitched GeoTIFF in Photoshop. Claim extended with §7: tile generation MUST be EPSG:3857 only — the CGL quadtree is defined on the Bing spherical Web-Mercator grid (2^z × 2^z, origin top-left, lat clip ±85.05°), so 4326/UTM/local-CRS sources must be reprojected before tiling or quadkeys land misaligned; the Piemonte ombreggiature WMS serves 3857 natively; ground resolution = 156543.03392/2^z × cos(lat) (z20 ≈ 0.1036 m/px at Domodossola ~46.1° N). §8: Photoshop/GIMP/Affinity all strip GeoTIFF tags (paint.net preserves them — rhumbaflappy's CGL loop uses it); the fix is a .tfw world-file sidecar (QGIS Translate advanced param tfw=yes, or gdal_translate -co TFW=YES -co PROFILE=BASELINE; 6-line format with top-left PIXEL CENTER per GDAL WLD driver), keep the pixel grid untouched in PS (no crop/resize), keep alpha on TIFF save (CGL blends in-game aerial via alpha), crop in QGIS before PS, validate alpha survives tiling.
